nodes.author: chidi1989
nodes.text:
emerged

As we step into 2025, reports indicate a surge in respiratory illnesses in China, including human metapneumovirus (HMPV), influenza A, and others. Hospitals are overwhelmed, reminding us that disease outbreaks can and do originate outside Africa.

nodes.author: chidi1989
nodes.text: Let’s not forget the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, which originated in Wuhan, China, and swept across the globe. While the world united to tackle the virus, Africa faced stigma despite managing the outbreak with fewer resources but remarkable efficiency.

nodes.author: chidi1989
nodes.text:
Historically, many pandemics emerged from the Global North:

Spanish Flu (1918): Likely originated in the U.S.

Swine Flu (2009): First identified in North America.

COVID-19 (2019): Originated in China.

Africa wasn’t the source of these devastating outbreaks.

nodes.author: chidi1989
nodes.text: Yet, the world repeatedly paints Africa as a continent “waiting for the next plague.” Why? This narrative is deeply rooted in colonial stereotypes, ignoring Africa’s proactive contributions to global health.

nodes.author: chidi1989
nodes.text: Diseases thrive where systems fail, not because of geography. Industrialized nations are not immune to outbreaks. Rapid urbanization, global trade, and deforestation—often driven by the West—are critical factors behind the rise of zoonotic diseases.

nodes.author: chidi1989
nodes.text:
As China grapples with its flu outbreak this year, let’s remind the world:

Africa is not the world’s scapegoat for disease.

Pandemics are global problems requiring collective solutions.

Stigmatizing one region doesn’t solve public health crises—it worsens them.
@elonmusk
